not_this.claim: Older pictures show Elasmosaurus with its head on the tail, which is wrong.
not_this.quote: Cope originally reconstructed the skeleton of Elasmosaurus with the skull at the end of the tail, an error which was made light of by the paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh, and became part of their "Bone Wars" rivalry.

not_this.claim: Older pictures show Elasmosaurus holding its neck high above the water, which is wrong.
not_this.quote: Contrary to earlier depictions, their necks were not very flexible, and could not be held high above the water surface.

not_this.claim: Older pictures show Elasmosaurus with a short neck and a long tail, which is wrong.
not_this.quote: The reconstruction showed Elasmosaurus with a short neck and a long tail, unlike other plesiosaurs, and Cope was also unsure whether it had hind limbs.

debated.claim: It is uncertain how many teeth Elasmosaurus had.
debated.quote: It is uncertain how many teeth Elasmosaurus had, due to the fragmentary state of the fossils.

debated.claim: The shape of the tail-fin is unknown.
debated.quote: Since the last tail-vertebrae of elasmosaurids were fused into a structure similar to the pygostyle of birds, it is possible this supported a tail-fin, but the shape it would have had is unknown.

second_reading.claim: The neck vertebrae were compressed sideways and had a longitudinal crest or keel along the sides.
second_reading.quote: Most of the neck vertebrae were compressed sideways, and bore a longitudinal crest or keel along the sides.
